name: Vienna Game
description: A flexible 1.e4 course that teaches the Vienna main setup first, then simple reactions to Black's common defenses.

branches.title: Main Line: Flexible Nc3
branches.description: Learn the default Vienna starting setup.

moves.title: Start with e4
moves.explanation: Control the center and open piece lines. e4 changes the central structure. Central pawn moves should either claim space, challenge an enemy pawn, or open a line for a piece. In the Vienna, support e4, develop quickly, and castle before turning the kingside space into an attack.

moves.title: Black mirrors
moves.explanation: Black also takes central space. e5 changes the central structure. Central pawn moves should either claim space, challenge an enemy pawn, or open a line for a piece. In the Vienna, support e4, develop quickly, and castle before turning the kingside space into an attack.

moves.title: Develop flexibly
moves.explanation: Nc3 supports e4 and keeps attacking ideas like f4 available later. Nc3 develops a knight to c3. Developed pieces control central squares, help castling, and make future tactics possible without forcing anything too early.

moves.title: Develop to f6
moves.explanation: Nf6 develops a knight to f6. Developed pieces control central squares, help castling, and make future tactics possible without forcing anything too early.

moves.title: Shape the center

moves.title: Develop to c5
moves.explanation: Bc5 develops a bishop to c5. Developed pieces control central squares, help castling, and make future tactics possible without forcing anything too early.

moves.title: Develop to f3
moves.explanation: Nf3 develops a knight to f3. Developed pieces control central squares, help castling, and make future tactics possible without forcing anything too early.

moves.title: Shape the center
moves.explanation: d6 changes the central structure. Central pawn moves should either claim space, challenge an enemy pawn, or open a line for a piece. In the Vienna, support e4, develop quickly, and castle before turning the kingside space into an attack.

moves.title: Develop to c4
moves.explanation: Bc4 develops a bishop to c4. Developed pieces control central squares, help castling, and make future tactics possible without forcing anything too early.

moves.title: Get the king safe
moves.explanation: O-O moves the king to safety and brings the rook closer to the center. This is usually the moment when the opening becomes an early middlegame plan: In the Vienna, support e4, develop quickly, and castle before turning the kingside space into an attack.

moves.title: Improve with h3
moves.explanation: h3 is a quiet improving move. Quiet moves matter when they finish development, prevent counterplay, or prepare a clear next plan.

moves.title: Improve with a6
moves.explanation: a6 is a quiet improving move. Quiet moves matter when they finish development, prevent counterplay, or prepare a clear next plan.

hints: Follow the highlighted move and say the idea out loud.
After each move, check king safety, center control, and piece activity.
When a trade appears, ask what file opens and which piece improves next.
coachingNotes: Learn the default Vienna starting setup.
In the Vienna, support e4, develop quickly, and castle before turning the kingside space into an attack.
Good trades usually remove an active enemy piece, open a useful file, or simplify once your king is safe.
After the opening, do not drift: improve your worst piece, connect rooks, and look for one clear pawn break.

moves.title: Trade or capture on e4
moves.explanation: Nxe4 shows how trades enter the opening. This capture should only be played because it gains time, opens lines, or solves a concrete problem. After a trade, ask which file opened and which piece should improve next.

moves.title: Put a rook to work
moves.explanation: Re1 activates a rook. Rooks belong on open or half-open files after trades, where they support the early middlegame plan.

ideas: Use Nc3 to support e4 and keep options open.
Against c5/c6/d5, respond with simple center and development rules.
Do not attack before the king is safe.
In the Vienna, support e4, develop quickly, and castle before turning the kingside space into an attack.
Trade only when it improves your position, removes danger, or opens a useful file.
By move 8-12, you should know your early middlegame plan: safe king, active pieces, and one central break.
commonMistakes: Stopping after memorized moves and playing without a plan.
Trading automatically without asking what improves afterward.
Starting an attack before castling or finishing development.
